title: Witness layouts: prove the transport once
source_text: \section{Witness layouts: prove the transport once}

title: The repeated argument
source_text:
\subsection{The repeated argument}

\src{Representation}{155--256} repeatedly proves that renaming input and
witness coordinates commutes with evaluation. In particular,
\code{Rep.conjunction} and \code{Rep.disjunction} each introduce the same
left and right evaluation equalities, using function extensionality and
case analysis. \code{reindex} and \code{existsBlock} contain closely
related arguments. A private one-sided helper also exists in
\src{QuarticCompiler}{95--98}; the proposal is to make the general
semantic law available at the representation layer.

The central law is:
\begin{Lean}
natAssignment v w ∘ Sum.map f g =
  natAssignment (v ∘ f) (w ∘ g)
\end{Lean}
Its proof is just \code{funext i; cases i <;> rfl}. Together with the
existing \code{Expr.eval_rename}, it eliminates the repeated left/right
transport proofs.

The second law is the existential equivalence between a single concatenated
witness block and its two components:
\begin{Lean}
(∃ w : Fin (m + n) → Nat,
  P (w ∘ Fin.castAdd n) (w ∘ Fin.natAdd m)) ↔
    ∃ a b, P a b
\end{Lean}
The forward map projects the two blocks. The reverse map uses
\code{Fin.addCases}. This works when either block has length zero, so
special empty-witness cases are unnecessary.

title: Preserve the executable data
source_text:
\subsection{Preserve the executable data}

The supplied \code{WitnessLayout.lean} defines compact conjunction and
disjunction constructors. Their witness counts are unchanged and their
expression fields are definitionally equal to the originals; the file
contains explicit \code{rfl} checks of expression equality. Thus the
proposal simplifies correctness proofs without changing the represented
polynomials, variable order, or number of witnesses.

The original two constructor declarations occupy 59 physical lines;
the compact versions occupy 32. This comparison excludes the shared
helper API. Its one-time cost must be included in a net repository
comparison, and it should be amortized across \code{reindex},
\code{existsBlock}, and further layout clients. The immediate gain is
conceptual: arithmetic correctness is no longer interrupted by repeated
function-coordinate bookkeeping.

title: Move existing projection lemmas to their natural home
source_text:
\subsection{Move existing projection lemmas to their natural home}

The desired witness-count simplification lemmas already exist in
\src{RepresentationSize}{136--147}, with graph analogues at lines
193--209. However, \src{DirectComposition}{59--68} still unfolds whole
constructors to compute counts. It cannot import the size module without
reversing the present dependency direction.

Move the small \code{rfl} projection lemmas next to the constructors or
into a lightweight module that imports only the constructors. The size
module can then concentrate on global bounds. This changes which facts
are available early, rather than adding duplicate facts. It also prevents
the simplifier from examining large expression and proof fields merely
to calculate a natural-number projection.

title: Checked histories and numeric scanners
source_text: \section{Checked histories and numeric scanners}

title: One invariant-preserving history fold
source_text:
\subsection{One invariant-preserving history fold}

The list processors in \code{AnnotatedRename}, \code{AnnotatedBound},
and \code{AnnotatedProofChecker} have the same recursive shape: validate
the next line against a history; prepend the emitted result; continue;
or reject. Rename and bound rows emit themselves; proof lines emit a
judgment. The appropriate abstraction therefore has two types and two
functions:

\begin{Lean}
def run (valid : Line → List Judgment → Bool)
    (emit : Line → Judgment) :
    List Line → List Judgment → Option (List Judgment)
  | [], seen => some seen
  | line :: lines, seen =>
      if valid line seen then
        run valid emit lines (emit line :: seen)
      else none
\end{Lean}

The generic soundness proof assumes exactly the local invariant step:
if all existing judgments satisfy \(P\), and a line passes validation,
then its emitted judgment satisfies \(P\). Induction on the remaining
lines proves the invariant for the final history.

The duplicated clusters are \src{AnnotatedRename}{196--235},
\src{AnnotatedBound}{136--175}, and
\src{AnnotatedProofChecker}{206--250}. They contain \code{run_append},
\code{run_sound}, \code{Produces.append}, and \code{Produces.step}.
The supplied \code{ValidatedFold.lean} proves the shared versions.
The existing \code{Produces} interface is useful; its implementation and
laws should become shared while public module-local names remain thin
specializations. Formula-specific soundness remains in the current row
or line soundness theorem.

A conservative migration keeps the old executable \code{run} definitions
and proves their equality with the common fold. A later migration may
replace those definitions by transparent specializations, but only after
checking any syntax-sensitive size claims. Extensional equality of
programs does not imply equality of their encoded abstract syntax trees.

title: Separate recurrence from encoding
source_text:
\subsection{Separate recurrence from encoding}

Five scanner modules independently establish the same iterator equations:
\code{AnnotatedRenameScan}, \code{AnnotatedBoundScan},
\code{AnnotatedLineScan}, \code{AnnotatedAxiomContext}, and
\code{AnnotatedContext}. Their \code{scan_succ} and fixed-terminal-state
proofs depend on iteration, not on pairing codes or formulas.

For an arbitrary state type, define
\begin{Lean}
def scan (step : State → State) (fuel : Nat)
    (initial : State) : State :=
  fuel.rec initial (fun _ acc => step acc)
\end{Lean}
Then prove once:
\begin{Lean}
scan step (fuel + 1) initial = scan step fuel (step initial)
step fixed = fixed → scan step fuel fixed = fixed
\end{Lean}
The two supplied recurrence proofs compile without any axioms.
They can replace the repeated induction proofs while preserving the old
numeric definitions through transparent unfolding.

The next stage is to share the simulation between encoded lists and typed
folds. Concrete targets are \src{AnnotatedRenameScan}{71--87},
\src{AnnotatedBoundScan}{67--83}, \src{AnnotatedLineScan}{132--152},
and \src{AnnotatedAxiomContext}{130--151}. The common simulation should
take a \code{step_cons} equation, an acceptance test, a history update,
and terminal/rejection encodings.

Two details are essential. Ordinary histories use zero as the empty code,
whereas an empty quoted context uses one. Also, correctness for raw codes
must continue to cover malformed inputs and arbitrary supplied fuel.
Proving only the behavior of well-typed encodings would weaken that contract.

title: A better primitive-recursive iterator interface
source_text:
\subsection{A better primitive-recursive iterator interface}

\src{DirectScalarArithmetic}{103--107} already provides
\code{iterate}, with a fixed numeric seed. The useful extension is
\code{iterateFrom}, accepting realized seed and fuel functions, plus a
parameterized step that can still access the original input. The repeated
constructions occur in \src{AnnotatedContextPR}{47--54},
\src{AnnotatedBoundScan}{144--158}, \src{AnnotatedLineScan}{231--245},
and \src{AnnotatedRenameScanPR}{48--75}.

The result should remain an explicit \code{R f} object with supplied
program data. A bare existence theorem \code{Nat.Primrec f} would lose
the data needed by the compiler and its size accounting. The expensive
validator is deliberately used once in
\src{AnnotatedLineScan}{201--226}; preserve that sharing. Require
equality of the constructed \code{.val} program, or recheck the exact
node-count theorems, before claiming unchanged encoded size.

title: Share tag dispatch and Boolean reflection
source_text:
\subsection{Share tag dispatch and Boolean reflection}

\src{AnnotatedRenameLocal}{63--87} and
\src{AnnotatedBoundLocal}{55--79} repeat the same tag partition:
\(0\)--\(1\), \(2\), \(3\)--\(5\), \(6\)--\(7\), and rejection for
tags at least \(8\). A single arithmetic dispatch lemma can certify that
the threshold implementation matches this partition, parameterized by
the four branch results.

The scanner interface can also be strengthened from an acceptance
equivalence to an exact value equation. Combine
\code{check = 1 ↔ valid = true} and
\code{check = 0 ∨ check = 1} into \code{check = truth valid}.
This removes repeated true/false reasoning in the two \code{step_cons}
proofs. The range premise is essential: the acceptance equivalence alone
allows a rejecting numeric result of two.

title: One executable sum-of-squares API
source_text:
\subsection{One executable sum-of-squares API}

Three modules contain equivalent private
\code{eval_sumExpressions} proofs:
\src{DAGQuartic}{83--86}, \src{NaturalDAGQuartic}{110--113}, and
\src{QuadraticRegisterSystem}{70--73}. Each then proves that a finite
sum of squared residuals is zero exactly when each residual is zero,
using the same \code{List.ofFn}, finite-sum conversion, and ordered-ring
lemma. Their degree proofs also repeat the same sum and product bounds.

Introduce a public expression constructor and three reusable theorems:
\begin{Lean}
def sumSquares (rows : Fin n → Expr σ) : Expr σ :=
  QuarticSyntax.sumExpressions
    (List.ofFn fun i => rows i * rows i)

(sumSquares rows).eval v = 0 ↔
  ∀ i, (rows i).eval v = 0

(∀ i, (rows i).toPolynomial.totalDegree ≤ d) →
  (sumSquares rows).toPolynomial.totalDegree ≤ 2 * d

(∀ e ∈ es, e.binaryOps ≤ b) →
  (QuarticSyntax.sumExpressions es).binaryOps ≤
    (b + 1) * es.length
\end{Lean}

The first equivalence is over integers, or another suitable ordered
structure where a sum of squares vanishes termwise. It is not valid over
an arbitrary commutative ring. The supplied prototype deliberately uses
integer evaluation. The degree statement is an upper bound, so it does
not claim an exact degree in the presence of cancellation.

The cost generalization also absorbs the existing special case with
row cost five in \src{QuarticCost}{60--65}, and the general argument
repeated in \code{DAGQuartic}. Because the expression uses the same
ordered list of squared residuals as before, clients can retain the exact
syntax rather than replacing it by an algebraically equivalent polynomial.

Signed witness reconstruction and natural witness reconstruction need
different hypotheses. Share residual aggregation first; a fully generic
signed/natural encoding framework should be attempted only if its
instantiation overhead is smaller than the duplication it replaces.

title: The semiring theorem already subsumes the natural induction
source_text:
\subsection{The semiring theorem already subsumes the natural induction}

\src{QuarticCompiler}{101--167} proves natural gate completeness and
soundness by syntax induction. \src{GatesSemiring}{72--145} proves the
corresponding results over an arbitrary commutative semiring, covering
the natural case. The two expression interpretations are already
connected by \code{Expr.eval_eq_zero_iff_splitNatural} and
\code{NatExpr.evalSemiring_nat}.

The useful refactor is architectural. Extract gate data, wire indexing,
roots, residual syntax, and value definitions into a lightweight module.
Prove generic gate semantics above it. Then derive the natural-number
results through the interpretation bridge, retaining their public names.
Currently \code{GatesSemiring} imports \code{QuarticCompiler}; simply
calling the generic theorem from the compiler would introduce a cycle.
Moving the data is the prerequisite.

Likewise, \src{QuadraticRegisterSystem}{18--33} implements an
unweighted degree and its polynomial bound, while
\src{WeightedExpressionDegree}{37--62} already proves the generic
weighted result. Constant weight one supplies the old bound. Keep an
abbreviation or compatibility equality if downstream proofs depend on
the old recursive equations. The polynomial-renaming theorem in
\code{QuarticCompiler.Gates} belongs in the expression API for the same
reason: basic syntax laws should be available without importing a compiler.

title: Generated circuit proofs: use the existing certificates

title: Where the source volume comes from
source_text:
\subsection{Where the source volume comes from}

\code{GapCircuitSteps66.lean} contains 484 local-step theorems and 86
power theorems. \code{SplitCircuitSteps59.lean} contains 515 step theorems
and 107 power theorems. Together they occupy 6,567 physical lines.
Every local-step theorem already calls the generic
\code{ArithmeticDAG.run_node_equation}; that theorem is not missing.
The repository also already has \code{run_eq_of_node_equations},
\code{value_eq_of_node_equations}, \code{run_power}, and a certified
power-sharing rewrite. The opportunity is to adopt these existing
interfaces consistently at the generated clients.

title: Replace 193 power chains by parent exponent certificates
source_text:
\subsection{Replace 193 power chains by parent exponent certificates}

The old power sections occupy 685 and 853 lines respectively, for a
combined 1,538 lines. Each chain follows multiplication nodes and proves
an exponent identity. The existing \code{run_power} theorem in
\src{ArithmeticDAGPowers}{26--46} abstracts exactly this argument.

Assign a natural exponent label \(\ell(i)\) to each node. Label zero
means that the node is outside the certified pure-power fragment.
The distinguished base has label one. Each labeled non-base node must
be a multiplication of earlier labeled nodes, with
\[
\ell(i)=\ell(a)+\ell(b).
\]
The literal node table is finite, so these local conditions are checked
by \code{decide +kernel}. Topology and the existing theorem then yield
\[
\operatorname{value}(i)=\operatorname{value}(\mathrm{base})^{\ell(i)}.
\]

The supplied \code{GapPowerCertificate.lean} and
\code{SplitPowerCertificate.lean} keep the original
\code{naturalNodes} exactly. They are proof certificates for those
circuits, not optimized replacement circuits. Their initial source
representation occupies 117 lines including label tables and examples,
compared with the 1,538-line old power component. This is a component
comparison; it is not a measured integrated project reduction. Existing
named callers must be migrated or retained as thin compatibility wrappers.
The supplied metrics record the concrete versions included in the archive.

For Split, all 515 entries of the proposed label table agree with the
old-label table already present in
\src{SplitJointPower59}{64--78}. Move that parent certificate to a small
shared module rather than importing an unrelated child circuit solely to
reuse its labels. The Python generator checks labels against the actual
multiplication nodes as a diagnostic. The Lean certificate is the proof.

Do not infer a compilation speedup from the shorter source. One finite
certificate can still be expensive to reduce. Compare actual replay time,
proof object size, and peak memory before choosing its final chunking.

title: Specialize low-level node equations at use sites
source_text:
\subsection{Specialize low-level node equations at use sites}

The supplied \code{CircuitDispatch.lean} wraps the generic node equation
in one \code{step p x i hi} theorem. At a concrete index, its type reduces
to the same scalar equation as \code{natural_step_i}. A short example
uses six selected node equations to prove the base identity
\(p_0(x_0+1)^2\).

This creates an alternative to eagerly declaring all 999 low-level
wrappers. However, replacing every short theorem name by a verbose
specialization can make clients harder to read. The practical compromise
is a small local elaboration helper or generator that emits applications
of the existing theorem, together with named results at meaningful
register boundaries.

Do not make unrestricted node expansion a global simplification rule.
Unfolding all shared registers recursively can turn a DAG into a large
expression tree. The named base, kernel, mask, rank, and source bindings
in \code{GapCircuitRegisters66} and \code{GapCircuitRecipe66} are useful
proof boundaries. Keep those boundaries, and reduce the repetitive
low-level transport beneath them.

title: A stronger half-radix lemma
source_text:
\subsection{A stronger half-radix lemma}

For all natural \(a,b\) and positive \(s\),
\[
\boxed{\quad
(sa)\bmod(2s)+\left\lfloor\frac{sb}{2s}\right\rfloor
=s(a\bmod2)+\left\lfloor\frac b2\right\rfloor.
\quad}
\]
The proof cancels a common positive factor in the modulus and quotient.
The Lean proof uses \code{Nat.mul_mod_mul_left} and
\code{Nat.mul_div_mul_left}, after commuting \(2s\).

Since \(a\bmod2\leq1\), the expression is at most \(s+1\) whenever
\(b\leq3\), with no bound on \(a\). If \(s\) is even, the expression's
parity equals \(\lfloor b/2\rfloor\) under the same bound on \(b\).
Without that bound, the parity is instead
\(\lfloor b/2\rfloor\bmod2\).

This replaces the four-case bound proof in
\src{NativeCyclicRotation}{100--116} and the sixteen combinations used
for parity at lines 160--165. The original proof bodies occupy 15 and
four nonblank lines; proposed wrappers are one-line applications of the
generic lemmas. Their helper cost must still be counted, so this is a
local simplification and strengthening, not automatically a net line
saving across the whole project.

\code{NativeRefactorCore.lean} checks the identity, bound, and parity
lemmas using only Lean's core arithmetic infrastructure. The supplied
\code{NativeRotationWrappers.lean} shows their intended applications to
the actual \code{shiftDigits}; its integration status is stated in the
validation ledger. The already generic Boolean rotation API in
\code{NativeBooleanRotation} remains useful and does not need replacement.

title: Share physical-field residue calculations
source_text:
\subsection{Share physical-field residue calculations}

The addition/subtraction residue proofs in
\src{CurrentClause2011}{27--39} are repeated privately in
\src{CurrentReflectedGeometry2011}{74--86}. A small
\code{CyclicFieldArithmetic} module should own these facts for total
length \(NL\) and field width \(L\). For an aligned base \(b\), field
offset \(e<L\), and arbitrary natural shift \(t\), a useful normal form is
\[
(b+e-t).\operatorname{val}\bmod L
=\bigl(L+e-(t\bmod L)\bigr)\bmod L.
\]
The positional subtraction on the left is in \(\mathbb Z/(NL)\mathbb Z\).
The bounded natural subtraction on the right is safe because
\(t\bmod L<L\). This is already the substance of
\src{CurrentCellTranslation2011}{84--94}; extract it downward instead
of importing that later module backward and creating a cycle.

The clause and marker convolution proofs both calculate the residues
of shifts 18 and 2020, then use support exclusion. A shared residue
normal form and support-zero helper would replace repeated arithmetic
with one instantiation and a small numerical check. The origin-exclusion
step in the corresponding mask lemmas can also be shared.

A particularly direct reuse is available for reflected coefficients.
\src{CurrentClause2011}{122--130} proves the residue modulo 2048.
\src{CurrentEarlyPadding2011}{95--107} reproves the corresponding
modulo-16 result by cases. After sharing the identical selector-unit
definition, project the stronger congruence using
\code{.of_dvd (by decide : 16 ∣ 2048)}.

Preserve arbitrary shifts, wraparound, and \(N=1\). A later equivalence
between aligned cells and \code{ZMod N} could simplify reindexing, but
the immediate extraction does not require a new coordinate representation.

title: Decode source-register equations once
source_text:
\subsection{Decode source-register equations once}

Several Pell arguments reconstruct the same raw arithmetic equations:
\[
q=1+J\beta,\qquad L=q^2-1,\qquad
N=q(1+L)=q^3,\qquad X=qw.
\]
Concrete repetitions occur in \code{source_Y_ge_two},
\code{source_rank_eq_target}, and \code{source_scale_eq} in
\src{NativePellBootstrap}{95--115, 415--436, 498--518}, and in
\src{NativePellPower}{127--143}. Main and auxiliary classifications
also decode related norm rows separately.

Extend the existing source-register helper approach to a small set of
named arithmetic facts proved once from the literal rows. State the
primitive identities over integers and derive natural-number corollaries
with explicit nonnegativity premises where subtraction is involved.
Pell arguments then consume semantic equations, with fewer row unfoldings
and casts.

Keep raw row equations, positivity, port bounds, Pell classification, and
rank recovery in separate interfaces. Bundling all of them together can
silently add assumptions to clients. The existing \code{PortBox} already
packages port inequalities; a differently named replacement adds no value.

title: Derive recurrence instead of storing it twice
source_text:
\subsection{Derive recurrence instead of storing it twice}

The existing \code{CurrentPolynomialWindow2011.Facts} record stores a
digit bound, a quotient recurrence, and an exact local decomposition.
The quotient recurrence follows from the other two. In natural arithmetic,
\[
u=d+rk,\quad d<r
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
k=\lfloor u/r\rfloor,\quad d=u\bmod r.
\]
The strict digit bound already implies \(r>0\). No extra positivity
assumption is needed in the generic implication.

The checked \code{CarryCertificate} prototype stores carry bounds,
digit bounds, and decomposition, indexed by the existing arrays and
predecessor function. Its \code{recurrence} theorem is a derived method.
In the current window, take
\(u_i=\operatorname{convolution}_i+
\operatorname{rotation}_i+k_{i-1}\).

This reduces repeated argument lists in
\src{CurrentPhaseParity2011}{92--163} and the parallel fields in
\src{CurrentPolynomialWindow2011}{27--65}. It also makes explicit which
facts are independent. Construct the record using the existing
normalization theorem obtained from the actual polynomial. A convenient
record must not become a new unproved assumption in place of that
construction.

Preserve minimal low-level statements. Some carry-reset lemmas need only
decomposition and carry bounds, without a digit bound or recurrence.
Keep those lemmas general and offer record-based wrappers to larger
clients. Changing every theorem to demand a large certificate would
shorten notation while strengthening hypotheses unnecessarily.

title: Keep checked finite chunks; share their assembly
source_text:
\subsection{Keep checked finite chunks; share their assembly}

\src{WangTiles942Data}{210--321} proves
\code{action_eq_decoder} by repeatedly splitting an index into successive
16-entry ranges. Its rail-cache counterpart repeats the pattern at
lines 439--512. Each branch reconstructs a local index, proves bounds,
and transports an already checked chunk equality.

The generic dispatcher in \code{NativeRefactorCore.lean} uses Euclidean
division below \(Bq\), and subtraction in the final tail:
\[
i=B\lfloor i/B\rfloor+(i\bmod B),\qquad
i<Bq+r.
\]
It combines \(q\) complete blocks of size \(B\) and a final block of
size \(r\). The action table uses \((B,q,r)=(16,26,14)\); the rail
table uses \((16,13,8)\). A small finite case selection can then choose
the already authenticated chunk theorem. An estimated 90--120 lines
could be removed across these two dispatchers, after helper overhead;
this is an estimate awaiting an integrated patch.

The same principle applies to the hand-built sum assembly in
\src{CurrentKernel2011}{156--419}. Keep the manageable independently
checked chunks, but describe their combination as data and apply one
proved aggregation theorem. A list of partial totals is enough to
generate a balanced assembly tree if reduction cost warrants it.

Do not replace kernel-checked leaves with \code{native_decide}. Native
evaluation adds a compiler-dependent axiom to the proof's trust boundary,
as documented by the official Lean reference. Nor should one assume that
a single enormous \code{decide +kernel} call is cheaper than the present
chunks. Compression should remove repeated assembly logic while retaining
the ability to control kernel reduction size.

title: One copied-field bound interface
source_text:
\subsection{One copied-field bound interface}

\src{CurrentCellLabels2011}{66--77, 283--299} reconstructs the same
four copied-field bounds, using offsets and widths
\((978,8),(960,9),(969,8),(942,9)\). The convolution-word proof repeats
the corresponding four block instantiations.

A small first step is \code{copiedFields_bounded}, returning the four
facts once. If more clients emerge, use a finite field descriptor with
offset, width, and packed shift, plus a generic field evaluation/bound
theorem. Preserve the actual order: packed fields are west, north, east,
south, whereas the \code{ColorsBounded} conclusion orders west, east,
north, south. A broad tuple refactor must handle that difference explicitly.

title: Object-language proofs: centralize the semantic boundary
source_text: \section{Object-language proofs: centralize the semantic boundary}

title: A shared bridge from arbitrary models to sealed derivations
source_text:
\subsection{A shared bridge from arbitrary models to sealed derivations}

There are 27 occurrences of \code{completeness_inf_context} in 18
\code{Object*.lean} files. Twenty-five follow the direct pattern of
extracting a model's ZF axioms, proving semantic validity, and applying
universal closure. Examples include
\src{ObjectNaturalExpression}{181--202},
\src{ObjectMultiplication}{198--215}, and
\src{ObjectAdditionLaws}{183--206}.

The following is the intended interface, not an assertion that this
particular integration theorem has been replayed:
\begin{Lean}
theorem zfc_proves_seal_of_zf_valid (φ : Form)
    (hφ : ∀ (V : Type) (mem : V → V → Prop),
      ZFAxioms mem → ∀ ee : Nat → V, Sat mem ee φ) :
    BProv ZFCax_s [] (sealF φ)
\end{Lean}

Its proof owns completeness, the extraction of axioms from a ZFC model,
and \code{seal_valid}. Each arithmetic client supplies only its
semantic validity theorem. The private model-extraction proof in
\src{ObjectArithmetic}{143--164} and public copy in
\src{ObjectMultiplication}{169--183} can be consolidated at a low
dependency layer. A later upstream helper already exists, but importing
the much heavier bounded-consistency layer into early arithmetic merely
to save a few lines would be a poor dependency tradeoff.

Keep the quantification over arbitrary models visible. Their internal
natural numbers may be nonstandard. Replacing their arithmetic by Lean's
ordinary \code{Nat} would change the theorem. The existing
\code{ObjectOmegaSemiring}, \code{ObjectNaturalOrderedSemiring}, and
\code{ObjectNaturalSemiring.evalRel_iff} already provide the relevant
internal algebra; adding semiring instances is not a new recommendation.

Likewise, \code{ObjectNaturalExpression.evalRel_unique} currently has
no natural-input guard. A typed semiring specialization with stronger
input hypotheses does not subsume that theorem. Preserve its current
generality separately.

title: Generalize closed-sentence transport across arity
source_text:
\subsection{Generalize closed-sentence transport across arity}

\src{ObjectQuarticCompiler}{100--116} defines a local \code{closed}
helper for the source arity and then repeats the proof for the target
arity. Quantify over an arbitrary arity \(k\), with argument
\code{(f : Expr (Fin k))}.
The target becomes another application of the same theorem.

Preferably expose the result as
\code{ObjectPolynomial.sat_noZeroForm_at_iff}, parallel to the existing
environment-specific consistency lemmas in \code{ObjectConsistency}
and \code{ObjectCodeSeal}. This is a narrow reusable interface for
closed formulas; it does not require redesigning the object language.

title: Adoption plan and criteria
source_text: \section{Adoption plan and criteria}

title: Stage 1: proof-only edits and shared laws
source_text:
\subsection{Stage 1: proof-only edits and shared laws}

Start with the lookup patch. Next introduce witness-layout transport,
sum-of-squares aggregation, and generic scan recurrences. Preserve old
declaration names and executable definitions, adding compatibility lemmas
where needed. Check the expression and program data before spending time
on shorter tactic scripts: \code{rfl} equality is the strongest convenient
result when it is available.

Each review should report old and new source lines including the shared
helper, the affected statements, and the axiom set of the public endpoints.
Do not count a common helper as free. Some APIs pay back only after their
second or third client migrates.

title: Stage 2: reuse certificates and reduce generated wrappers
source_text:
\subsection{Stage 2: reuse certificates and reduce generated wrappers}

Move parent exponent certificates into reusable modules and replace power
chains in the old generated proofs. Retain thin aliases during migration
if that keeps downstream changes small. Then introduce scoped node
specialization beneath the named semantic register lemmas. Measure source
bytes as well as lines, because dense certificate tables make physical
line counts sensitive to formatting.

For finite tables, keep the checked leaf size initially and change only
the dispatcher or sum assembly. Rechunking and changing the mathematical
representation should be separate changes, so a performance regression
has an identifiable cause.

title: Stage 3: reorganize dependencies and object transport
source_text:
\subsection{Stage 3: reorganize dependencies and object transport}

Move basic constructor projection laws down the import graph. Split gate
data from generic semantics before replacing natural syntax inductions.
Extract shared cyclic-field arithmetic, source-register equations, and
the arbitrary-model bridge into appropriately early modules. Then migrate
clients incrementally, preserving minimal assumptions at low levels.

Avoid importing the aggregate \code{DiophantineConsistency} module into
a small proof that needs only one or two leaf APIs. This is an engineering
recommendation based on the aggregate's broad import list, not a measured
claim about any particular build's bottleneck.

title: Profile a concrete bottleneck rather than increasing budgets
source_text:
\subsection{Profile a concrete bottleneck rather than increasing budgets}

The source contains many heartbeat and recursion-depth settings. Those
are candidate locations to inspect, not proof that those files are slow.
For a representative theorem, record elaboration time, kernel-checking
cost where available, peak memory, and generated object size under the
same compiler, cache state, and concurrency. Use the pinned compiler's
profiling tools and narrow the measurement to a declaration or module.

Prefer stable semantic rewrites and a small \code{simp only} vocabulary
at a large interface. During development, use search or suggested
simplifications to discover the right facts, then keep the resulting
proof explicit. Global simplification rules that unfold full circuits,
entire source-row systems, or encoded syntax can erase the very sharing
that makes the proof tractable.

\subsection{What the checks establish}

An exit-zero Lean compilation checks the supplied declaration's proof
in its stated environment. The expression-equality examples in the
witness prototype additionally check the proposed constructors' literal
expression data. The power prototypes, when marked passed in the ledger,
use the original circuit definitions and validate their exponent-label
conditions in Lean. Python's parallel label checks are diagnostics and
do not enlarge the trusted proof base.

The lookup patch is distinct: the two generic proof terms compile and
the patch applies cleanly, but the five entire modified modules have
not been replayed. The other large refactorings are source-grounded
designs or standalone theorem prototypes. No whole-project shortened
variant has been built, and no whole-project speedup or reduction
percentage is claimed.

title: Logical boundaries to retain
source_text:
\subsection{Logical boundaries to retain}

Several source facts constrain any simplification:
\begin{itemize}
\item \code{NativeFieldCycles2011.offset19_excludes_510} excludes value
510. The genuine 511 self-loop satisfies its assumptions and is tested
in the existing checks. A replacement claiming that every nonzero cycle
is impossible would be false.
\item The offset-20 exclusion applies to an arbitrary function; it must
not gain a finiteness or permutation hypothesis merely to share a wrapper.
\item Cell-translation facts include wrapping, arbitrary large shifts,
and the one-cell case. Keep these concrete regression checks.
\item The maintained current polynomial's arithmetic window and the
pending copy/label/machine composition are different proof obligations.
Refactoring arithmetic interfaces does not complete the latter.
\item Ordinary host-level arithmetic, arbitrary-model internal naturals,
and syntactic ZFC derivability remain separate semantic layers.
\end{itemize}

These are specific properties of the reviewed source, not generic
restrictions on proof automation. They identify where a superficially
shorter proof could inadvertently weaken the intended result.

title: Primary sources
Executive assessment
source_text:
\section*{Executive assessment}

The best opportunities are to share the algebraic and semantic interfaces that
many existing proofs already implement. Replacing a substantial proof family
with one invariant is more valuable than shortening individual tactic scripts.
This development already contains good examples of that design: generic DAG
node semantics, an addition-chain certificate checker, semiring gate semantics,
and a structural proof of the actual tile permutation. Several other modules
still duplicate the interfaces around those results.

This study combines an inventory of the active Lean tree, close reading of
selected proof families, compiled refactoring prototypes, and reviewable patches.
The deliverable is deliberately explicit about the difference between a complete
patched module that has been checked, a checked generic helper whose downstream
migration is still proposed, and an architectural idea that has not been implemented.
It does not establish a new consistency equivalence or complete the remaining
current-equation formalization.

Two complete checked patches are supplied: the package-52 coefficient-bound
module decreases from 679 to 127 physical lines, and the representation module
from 260 to 245. The latter saves 23 nonblank declaration lines after charging
for its shared helpers. Six additional checked modules demonstrate the reusable
interfaces and exact-signature alternatives discussed below.

The principal recommendations are:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Replace the repeated coefficient-envelope proof trees by one finite row
  split and a fixed arithmetic proof schema, preserving the sharp envelope.
\item Share the natural-assignment renaming law in representation constructors.
  The checked alternatives preserve the exact expressions and witness counts.
\item Use a scaled quotient/remainder identity for half-radix rotation, and a
  common residue API for cyclic block positions.
\item Share scanner iteration invariants and weighted finite-fiber summation.
\item Reuse the existing DAG and power-certificate interfaces to reduce generated
  proof scaffolding, measuring elaboration before removing cached declarations.
\item Reorganize expression and gate-semantics modules so each structural
  induction has one owner.
\end{enumerate}

The two generated circuit-step files contain 6,567 physical lines. This is a
large source-maintenance opportunity, but those lines are generated expansions,
not 6,567 lines of distinct mathematical argument. No whole-project percentage
reduction or compilation speedup is claimed.

title: What counts as a useful simplification?
source_text:
\subsection{What counts as a useful simplification?}

Four costs should be tracked separately: maintained source, mathematical proof
structure, elaboration cost, and the transparency of the resulting theorem.
The practical objective is a smaller set of reusable invariants with explicit
interfaces. A one-line tactic that unfolds an enormous term can have worse
elaboration behavior and be harder to repair than a longer sequence of named lemmas.

Exact expression syntax and witness counts matter here. A merely equivalent
Diophantine representation can change the constants, size bounds, executable
recipe, or later calibration. The representation refactor therefore includes
equalities between the alternative constructors and the original constructors,
proved by reflexivity. The coefficient refactor retains the literal coefficient
function and the original envelope. The arithmetic interfaces keep all essential
positivity and cyclic-domain assumptions.

title: The repeated argument
source_text:
\subsection{The repeated argument}

\src{Representation} repeatedly establishes that renaming input and witness
indices commutes with the natural-to-integer assignment. The same calculation
appears in \code{Rep.reindex}, twice in \code{Rep.conjunction}, and twice in
\code{Rep.disjunction}. The underlying law is
\[
  \operatorname{natAssignment}(v,w)\circ\operatorname{Sum.map}(f,g)
  =\operatorname{natAssignment}(v\circ f,w\circ g).
\]
Its proof is function extensionality followed by the two constructors of a sum.
Composing it with the existing \code{Expr.eval_rename} produces the semantic
interface used at every call site.

\begin{lstlisting}
theorem natAssignment_comp_sumMap (v : tau -> Nat) (w : beta -> Nat)
    (f : sigma -> tau) (g : alpha -> beta) :
    Function.comp (natAssignment v w) (Sum.map f g) =
      natAssignment (Function.comp v f) (Function.comp w g) := by
  funext i
  cases i <;> rfl
\end{lstlisting}
The complete, compilable source is \code{Lean/ProofSimplification/RepresentationNaturality.lean}.

The reindex correctness proof becomes an explicit simplification using the
shared evaluation lemma. Conjunction and disjunction retain their existing
\code{Fin.addCases} witness assembly. Their mathematical constructions are
unchanged; only the repeated assignment calculation is centralized.

title: Why this is a substantial local target
source_text:
\subsection{Why this is a substantial local target}

\src{NativeCoefficientBounds} has 679 physical lines. Its documented subject
is the package-52 native parent. Thus the largest measured local reduction
belongs to that existing arithmetic layer; the current length-2011 calibration
has separate field and mask proofs. A large part of the file
is the family \code{rowEnvelope_0} through \code{rowEnvelope_21}, followed by a
public wrapper. Each private proof repeats three positivity facts and follows
the conditional coefficient recipe through a tree of absolute-value bounds.
The repeated region contains 158 occurrences of the same restricted
\texttt{\detokenize{linarith only}} closure and 136 applications of \code{abs_ite_le}.

Write the four ports as $b,t,m,f$, where $t$ is the large transport parameter.
The exact envelope is
\[
 E=2b^2+2fb+m+f+2b+tb+t+8.
\]
Given $b,t,m,f\geq0$, the proof uses only those four inequalities and
$b^2\geq0$, $fb\geq0$, $tb\geq0$. Once a coefficient branch is exposed, both
sides of its absolute-value inequality are linear combinations of these
quantities. Restricted linear arithmetic is therefore sufficient.

title: The proposed replacement structure
source_text:
\subsection{The proposed replacement structure}

Keep the original definition of \code{envelope} and the actual
\code{rowCoefficient}. Introduce the three shared nonnegativity facts once.
Split the 22-valued row index, reduce that row's definition, and traverse its
conditional tree with the existing semantic helper \code{abs_ite_le}.
One \texttt{\detokenize{repeat' apply abs_ite_le}} replaces the manually written branch tree.
At every leaf, rewrite \code{abs_le} and solve the two inequalities with the
same fixed collection of facts.

This removes proof duplication while retaining the sharp dependence on the
transport port. In particular, the refactor does not replace the envelope by a
convenient but larger quadratic expression in $t$. The downstream
\code{envelope_lt} estimate and correction bound keep their mathematical content.

\CoeffStatus

The shared proof body is:
\begin{lstlisting}
have hsq := sq_nonneg (ports 0)
have hmf := mul_nonneg h3 h0
have hkp := mul_nonneg h1 h0
fin_cases k <;>
  simp only [rowCoefficient, envelope,
    Matrix.cons_val_zero', Matrix.cons_val_succ'] <;>
  repeat' apply abs_ite_le
all_goals
  rw [abs_le]
  constructor <;>
    linarith only [h0, h1, h2, h3, hsq, hmf, hkp]
\end{lstlisting}

The supplied patch has a complete module copy, not just an isolated proof
fragment. Its public theorem has the same quantifiers, hypotheses, and conclusion.
The code-generating origin of coefficient data does not make the arithmetic
schema an oracle: branch reduction and \code{linarith} produce terms checked
by Lean's kernel.

title: Maintenance considerations
source_text:
\subsection{Maintenance considerations}

The choice of branch interface matters: a trial using generic
\code{split_ifs} reached a simplification-step limit on the longest row.
Applying the shared absolute-value lemma handles both branch values without
evaluating the pair-index equality tests or carrying their branch hypotheses.
This is a concrete example where a small semantic lemma makes the concise
proof more robust than unrestricted case splitting.

This proof depends deliberately on the finite recipe representation. If a row
changes, Lean rechecks its branches against the same envelope and fails if the
old bound no longer holds. Use \texttt{\detokenize{linarith only}} with the fixed sign facts,
so branch equalities do not become accidental proof dependencies. A named local
tactic can be helpful if several coefficient families use the identical
schema, but adding a general tactic framework for this one family is unnecessary.

A further, unimplemented improvement is to represent the repeated coefficient
values by a small finite catalog. The baseline's 136 nondefault branches have
25 distinct textual value expressions, plus the default zero. The row/pair
lookup would return a catalog
entry, and its envelope bound would be proved once per entry. A separate exact
evaluation theorem must identify the catalog lookup with the existing literal
coefficient function. That extra equality is what makes the catalog a proof
refactor rather than a changed arithmetic encoding. This is a larger generator
and data-layout change than the immediate proof-schema patch.

title: An exact identity removes finite digit enumeration
source_text:
\subsection{An exact identity removes finite digit enumeration}

For natural numbers $s,x,y$ with $s>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:scaled}
 (sx)\bmod(2s)+\left\lfloor\frac{sy}{2s}\right\rfloor
 =s(x\bmod2)+\left\lfloor\frac y2\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}
This follows directly from \code{Nat.mul_mod_mul_left} and
\code{Nat.mul_div_mul_left}. It is an equality for arbitrary $x,y$; no digit
bound is required. The assumption $s>0$ is essential: at $s=0$ the left side
is zero, whereas the right side need not be.

If $y\leq3$, then $x\bmod2\leq1$ and $y/2\leq1$, giving
\[
 (sx)\bmod(2s)+(sy)/(2s)\leq s+1.
\]
If $s$ is even as well, the parity of the same expression is exactly $y/2$.
These are \code{scaled_half_bound} and \code{scaled_half_parity} in the supplied
\code{ArithmeticRefactors} module. Notice that the bound on $x$ is unnecessary;
only the predecessor value $y$ needs its small-digit bound.

\src{NativeCyclicRotation} currently proves \code{shiftDigits_half_bound}
using four cases for the current digit and a separate quotient estimate.
Its \code{shiftDigits_half_parity_89} uses the sixteen combinations of two
four-valued digits. Equation~\eqref{eq:scaled} explains both arguments at once.
The supplied \code{RotationRefactors} alternatives use the same original theorem
signatures and retain the absence of a \texttt{\detokenize{NeZero n}} assumption. They do not
call the old bound or parity theorem.

\RotationStatus

The parity proof is not necessarily shorter as an isolated four-line script:
the original enumeration is already compactly written. The improvement is an
explicit reusable reason for the result, with less dependence on the particular
radix exponent or digit case count. Shared-helper overhead should be included
when assessing a one-off replacement.

title: Factor the correct cyclic residue statements
source_text:
\subsection{Factor the correct cyclic residue statements}

Near-identical block-residue proofs appear in \src{CurrentClause2011},
\src{CurrentReflectedGeometry2011}, \src{NativeLocalMask54}, and
\src{NativeCleanBands54}. The useful common parameter is the block length $L$,
with positions in $\mathbb Z/(NL)\mathbb Z$. The checked generic identities are
\[
 \operatorname{val}(b+e)\bmod L=(\operatorname{val}(b)+e)\bmod L,
\]
\[
 (\operatorname{val}(k-e)+e)\bmod L=\operatorname{val}(k)\bmod L.
\]
Both follow by casting into the full cyclic modulus, then restricting modular
equality along $L\mid NL$. The supplied statements use \texttt{\detokenize{[NeZero (N * L)]}}.

The subtraction identity is intentionally written with addition of $e$ after
taking the representative. Replacing cyclic subtraction by truncated natural
subtraction would break wrapped positions. A common arithmetic module can
export these facts below both the current and legacy calibration layers.
\src{CurrentCellTranslation2011} can then consume them while retaining its
explicit wrapped and unwrapped source-position theorems.

\checked: the generic residue and scaled-arithmetic lemmas compile. Migrating
every current and legacy caller is still a proposed follow-up. Their common
arithmetic does not identify the different masks, offsets, or tile calibrations.

title: Shared scanner machinery without changing raw-input soundness
source_text:
\section{Shared scanner machinery without changing raw-input soundness}

\src{AnnotatedAxiomContext}, \src{AnnotatedBoundScan},
\src{AnnotatedLineScan}, \src{AnnotatedContext}, and
\src{AnnotatedRenameScan} all define a numeric scanner by primitive recursion
on fuel. The transition function may have additional fixed parameters, but
after those are supplied it is an endofunction on states.

The checked \code{ScannerCore} defines exactly the existing recursion pattern:
\begin{lstlisting}
def scan (step : S -> S) (fuel : Nat) (initial : S) : S :=
  fuel.rec initial (fun _ acc => step acc)
\end{lstlisting}
It proves the successor law, preservation of a fixed state, preservation of an
invariant, and preservation of ``reject or good.'' All four axiom reports are
empty. Existing scanner definitions can remain unchanged and use these facts
by definitional equality; a supplied example checks the raw recursion directly.

For the soundness interface, let $r$ be the rejecting state and suppose
\[
 T(r)=r,\qquad G(s)\Longrightarrow T(s)=r\ \lor\ G(T(s)).
\]
Then starting from a good state, every fuel-bounded iterate is rejecting or
good. This is the invariant $P(s):=(s=r\lor G(s))$ under the ordinary iteration
theorem. The disjunction need not be exclusive.

For a concrete proof checker, $G$ can say that a raw numeric state encodes an
actual history of provable judgments. The transition proof must still establish
that invariant from the local checker result. It must not assume that arbitrary
raw inputs already parse as valid formulas or derivations. Likewise, the helper
does not prove termination, enough fuel, successful acceptance, or the
primitive-recursive realization of the scanner program. Those obligations
remain in the concrete modules.

The first migration should target \code{scan_zero}, \code{scan_succ}, and
\code{scan_done}; these are low-risk direct uses. Only then should the common
shape of \code{scan_sound} be factored, with the raw-input theorem and explicit
program code checked again. A change to a program constructor requires separate
attention to the existing code-size claims.

title: One finite-fiber identity for folded stencils
source_text:
\section{One finite-fiber identity for folded stencils}

\src{NativeCyclicConvolution} proves \code{mass_foldStencil},
\code{convolution_foldStencil}, and the finite-sum step inside
\code{word_foldStencil} by repeatedly swapping sums and collapsing an equality
filter. All are instances of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pushforward}
 \sum_{k\in K}\left(\sum_{i\in I:p(i)=k}a_i\right)w_k
 =\sum_{i\in I}a_iw_{p(i)}.
\end{equation}
The supplied \code{FinitePushforward.sum_fiber_mul} proves this for finite
index types, an arbitrary map $p:I\to K$, and a semiring. Multiplication need
not be commutative, because the order $a_iw_{p(i)}$ is retained. Decidable
equality on $K$ is used to express the finite filter.

Three specializations are immediate: $w_k=1$ for mass,
$w_k=c(q-k)$ for convolution at $q$, and $w_k=\rho^{\operatorname{val}(k)}$
for a word. For the last specialization, the existing
\code{pow_mod_length} argument is still required to replace the reduced
exponent by the original exponent modulo $\rho^n-1$.

\checked: the generic identity compiles. It assumes no injectivity of $p$,
so all collisions are retained. It does not establish no-carry bounds, mask
compatibility, or uniqueness of a word representation. A safe integration
replaces the repeated finite-sum rearrangement and preserves those separate
arithmetic obligations.

This is a useful example of a small abstraction with several interpretations.
It makes the collision behavior obvious at the interface instead of requiring
each proof reader to reconstruct it from a double sum.

title: Replace repetitive node interfaces selectively
source_text:
\subsection{Replace repetitive node interfaces selectively}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
Module & Physical lines & Node equations & Power equations\\
\midrule
\code{GapCircuitSteps66} & 3,122 & 484 & 86\\
\code{SplitCircuitSteps59} & 3,445 & 515 & 107\\
\midrule
Total & 6,567 & 999 & 193\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Both files explicitly identify themselves as generated. Their local node
equations already apply \code{ArithmeticDAG.run_node_equation} from
\src{ArithmeticDAGSemantics}. Thus the mathematical invariant is already shared;
the remaining duplication is the interface and its generated normalization.

\proposed: expose one theorem indexed by
\texttt{\detokenize{Fin naturalNodes.length}}, giving the local equation for that node.
At a use site, instantiate it and reduce only the selected node lookup.
Alternatively, a small proof-producing elaborator can perform those two steps.
The generator can retain named theorems at semantic boundaries such as the
base, a source quantity, or an output residual, while avoiding an independent
declaration for every routine node.

There is a concrete tradeoff. Existing named node equations cache their reduced
types. Replacing them by repeated lookup reduction against a large literal list
can make elaboration slower even if the source is shorter. A measured migration
should compare the downstream recipe modules, not just the step-file line count.
Compatibility aliases and newly emitted data must be counted in the final size.

title: The power-label checker is already available
source_text:
\subsection{The power-label checker is already available}

\src{ArithmeticDAGPowers} contains \code{PowerStep}, \code{run_power}, and
\code{value_eq_of_powerRewrite}. These establish soundness of a table of
exponent labels for the actual topological circuit. The generation scripts
already compute labels of this form: the base receives label one, and a
multiplication of two labelled predecessors receives the sum of their labels.

\proposed: emit the label table as data, prove its finite local obligations by
kernel-checked computation, and apply \code{run_power} once. Named powers can
then be short specializations. This is preferable to inventing a second
symbolic-power correctness mechanism or repeatedly invoking \code{ring} after
each predecessor rewrite.

The 193 generated power equations identify the candidate population; they are
not a promised 193-theorem net saving. The label data and API aliases have a
cost. The proof must retain the actual circuit, its topological order, the
correct base, operand labels, and index bounds. This migration has not been
implemented in the supplied patches.

title: Expression and compiler architecture
source_text: \section{Expression and compiler architecture}

title: Centralize residual-square semantics and degree bounds
source_text:
\subsection{Centralize residual-square semantics and degree bounds}

\src{DAGQuartic}, \src{NaturalDAGQuartic}, and
\src{QuadraticRegisterSystem} repeat an evaluator lemma for
\code{QuarticSyntax.sumExpressions} and a theorem that a finite sum of squared
integer residuals vanishes exactly when every residual vanishes. Their proofs
already use the library's \code{Finset.sum_mul_self_eq_zero_iff}.

\proposed: put list evaluation and the finite residual-square interface below
the three compiler layers. Each compiler then supplies only its own residual
family. A companion degree theorem should derive a quartic upper bound from
quadratic bounds on the residuals. This avoids reproving both the semantic
and polynomial-size bookkeeping for every witness-layout variant.

The zero-set theorem needs its mathematical domain. Over $\mathbb Z$ the
nonnegative squares cannot cancel. Over an arbitrary commutative ring the
statement can fail, so a ring-generic evaluator theorem is not by itself a
ring-generic residual-zero theorem. Use the existing ordered/integer interface
or state exactly the additional assumptions that a broader theorem needs.

title: Move basic syntax facts below the consumers
source_text:
\subsection{Move basic syntax facts below the consumers}

\code{QuarticCompiler.Gates.polynomial_rename} and
\code{NaturalRegisterRelation.rename_toPolynomial} have the same statement:
\[
 (\operatorname{rename}(f,e)).\operatorname{toPolynomial}
 =\operatorname{MvPolynomial.rename}(f,e.\operatorname{toPolynomial}).
\]
Both are structural induction proofs. A canonical theorem in the \code{Expr}
layer removes duplicate ownership; aliases can retain existing call sites.

Similarly, \code{QuadraticRegisterSystem.syntaxDegree} and
\code{polynomial_degree_le} concern expression syntax, not register execution.
Moving them into a low-level expression module allows all residual compilers
to use one syntactic degree bound. Such a bound is an upper bound; it must not
replace a semantic identity or an exact degree claim that depends on cancellation.

title: Share the gate soundness and completeness inductions
source_text:
\subsection{Share the gate soundness and completeness inductions}

\src{QuarticCompiler} contains natural/integer gate soundness and completeness
proofs. \src{GatesSemiring} contains parallel generic semiring proofs for the
same wire structure, root, and residual syntax. The existing import direction
is important: \code{GatesSemiring} imports \code{QuarticCompiler}.

\proposed migration:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Extract \code{Wire}, \code{root}, \code{count}, and \code{residualSyntax}
  into a dependency-light \code{GatesSyntax} module.
\item Put generic semiring evaluation, soundness, and completeness above that syntax.
\item Derive the natural/integer versions using existing
  \code{NatExpr.evalSemiring_nat} and
  \code{Expr.eval_eq_zero_iff_splitNatural}.
\item Retain the executable constructors and verify exact witness and operation counts.
\end{enumerate}
Simply calling a generic gate theorem from the current compiler without first
extracting syntax would create an import cycle. The real simplification is one
owner for each induction and short transport results at the boundaries.

title: Respect the object-language boundary
source_text:
\subsection{Respect the object-language boundary}

The \code{Object*} modules prove arithmetic facts inside the repository's
sealed ZFC calculus. \src{ObjectNaturalSemiring} ranges over the model's entire
internal natural numbers, including any nonstandard elements.
\src{ObjectResidualSquares} uses this interpretation to obtain an internal
residual-conjunction statement.

A proof about ordinary Lean naturals alone cannot replace such a theorem.
The useful refactor is to identify a generic algebraic statement that holds
for the already constructed internal semiring, then use the explicit semantic
and syntactic transport theorems. Avoid replacing internal assignments by
standard numerals or treating an external semantic proof as an internal
derivation. This boundary is central to preserving the intended consistency claim.

title: Further targeted opportunities
source_text: \section{Further targeted opportunities}

title: Bundle carry witnesses with named fields
source_text:
\subsection{Bundle carry witnesses with named fields}

\code{NativeWindowCarry.source_convolution_carries} and
\code{CurrentWindowCarry2011.source_carries} return carry and digit functions
with several nested facts: carry bounds, digit bounds, quotient recurrence,
the carrying equation, the reconstructed word, and mask compatibility.
Repeatedly unpacking these long conjunctions increases argument-management work.

\proposed: define a small record for the generic carry solution, with named
fields for the recurrence and bounded carries, then put source-specific word
and mask facts in a separate wrapper if needed. Where a digit is definitionally
the remainder, its bound and carrying equation should be derived once from
division with a positive radix. A record improves theorem navigation and makes
it harder to supply a fact about the wrong digit array.

The record must not collapse local carry reset into a global no-carry claim.
Nor should it introduce a hidden temporal-alignment premise. Those distinctions
are present in the current arithmetic and remain essential. This proposal is
about a clearer interface; no line reduction is measured for it yet.

title: Use standard membership lemmas for small inductions
source_text:
\subsection{Use standard membership lemmas for small inductions}

The private \code{AnnotatedProofChecker.mem_of_lookup} repeats a list/index
induction to infer $j\in\mathrm{seen}$ from
\texttt{\detokenize{seen[i]? = some j}}. The pinned core library already provides
\code{List.mem_of_getElem?}. The supplied \code{ListLookup} file checks the
corresponding generic theorem directly, with only \code{propext} in its axiom report.

This is a checked API-level cleanup, not a replayed patch to the entire annotated
checker. Its surrounding natural-deduction rule proof has genuinely distinct
cases. Explicit rule constructors can remain visible while standard list facts
discharge the repeated premise-membership obligations.

title: Use existing structural proofs as patterns
source_text:
\subsection{Use existing structural proofs as patterns}

Two recent modules already illustrate the intended direction.
\src{WangTiles942Permutation} proves a structural left inverse for the actual
tile table, then proves injectivity and rank properties. It does not perform a
quadratic comparison of every tile pair. \src{NativeFieldCycles2011} uses
periodicity and modular arithmetic to exclude the remaining offsets, including
a short two-step residue obstruction where no finiteness is needed.

These are existing achievements, not new results of this audit. They suggest a
method for future proofs: identify the structural inverse, invariant, or local
residue obstruction before generating a large finite case analysis. In
\src{CurrentKernel2011}, small batches of kernel-computed finite sums also serve
as deliberate elaboration boundaries. Removing those boundaries to obtain one
large decision call needs performance evidence.

source_text:
\section{Implementation order and validation policy}

\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.06\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.39\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.20\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.24\textwidth}}
\toprule
Stage & Change & Evidence in this package & Next integration step\\
\midrule\endhead
1 & Assignment naturality & Complete checked patch & Apply in a branch; replay direct consumers\\
1 & Coefficient envelope schema & Complete checked patch & Check downstream coefficient-bound consumers\\
1 & Residue and scaled arithmetic & Checked generic helpers & Migrate callers with original signatures\\
1 & List membership alias & Checked library API & Replay annotated checker\\
2 & Scanner fixed-point/iteration facts & Checked generic helper & Replace basic lemmas before soundness invariants\\
2 & Weighted finite fibers & Checked generic helper & Specialize mass, convolution, word sum step\\
2 & Expression renaming and residual-square API & Source-grounded proposal & Move low-level lemmas; retain aliases\\
3 & Gate semantics shared over semirings & Architecture proposal & Extract syntax first; avoid import cycle\\
3 & Indexed circuit steps and power labels & Existing checker identified & Pilot one recipe; measure elaboration and memory\\
3 & Carry record and generic block geometry & Interface proposal & Keep explicit source and phase obligations\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

For a proof-only patch, review the theorem statement and executable data first.
Then compile the complete changed module against the pinned dependencies,
inspect its axiom report, and replay the direct consumers that depend on its
API or reduction behavior. For a structural change, add an exact equality or
transport theorem when data preservation is part of the claim. Source-level
shortening by itself is not evidence that a witness representation is unchanged.

The included experiments check complete patched modules independently, so a
candidate is not accidentally accepted by importing the old theorem with the
same name. Additive prototypes can import old modules for definitions, but their
proofs must not invoke the old theorem they purport to replace. The rotation
alternatives meet this condition.

title: Trusted computation and simplification boundaries
source_text:
\subsection{Trusted computation and simplification boundaries}

The existing development uses kernel-checked finite computation. The suggested
certificate approach retains that property. Lean's documentation distinguishes
\texttt{\detokenize{decide +kernel}} from \code{native_decide}/\texttt{\detokenize{decide +native}}, which
uses native evaluation and changes the trusted dependencies of a proof
\cite{lean-tactics,lean-validate}. This report does not propose changing that
trust boundary to save source lines.

Use explicit semantic rewrite lemmas around representations, scopes, and
assignments. Lean's \texttt{\detokenize{simp only}} permits a deliberately bounded rewrite set
\cite{lean-simp}; it is useful at those interfaces. Broad simplification is
often appropriate for small constructor goals, but expanding an entire circuit
or coefficient recipe as a global simp rule can obscure the intended boundaries.

title: Validation results and reproducibility
source_text:
\section{Validation results and reproducibility}

The bundle contains source hashes, patch checks, compilation logs, and
machine-readable records of successful runs. The generic residue, scaled
arithmetic, finite-fiber, scanner, assignment, and list-lookup interfaces are
compiled with the pinned toolchain. The detailed status of each final source
is recorded in \code{validation/final-validation.json}.

The reported axiom sets for the new algebraic and representation proofs are
subsets of \{\code{propext}, \code{Classical.choice}, \code{Quot.sound}\}.
The four scanner lemmas require no axioms. No new \code{sorry}, custom axiom,
or native-evaluation oracle is used. A separate source review checked the
packaged generic interfaces for hidden hypothesis strengthening and circularity;
that review is included as an evidence note and is not described as a second
compilation run.

The complete DiophantineConsistency library and all downstream consumers were
not rebuilt. The generic scanner and finite-sum abstractions have not been
installed throughout the project. Architectural proposals remain proposals.
These limits are reflected in the status labels rather than being hidden by
the existence of a successful small example.

Individual compilation times are retained for reproducibility, not interpreted
as performance benchmarks. For example, one representation replay took 3.90 s
for the original and 5.01 s for the patched file under concurrent load. Those
observations do not demonstrate a speedup. Other checks ran under substantial
shared CPU and disk pressure. A serious performance comparison should isolate
the same complete target, use the same cached imports and output mode, repeat
runs, and report peak memory as well as elapsed time.

title: How to use the bundle
source_text:
\subsection{How to use the bundle}

Start from the pinned ProveIt checkout with its Lean dependencies available.
The \code{README.md} describes the exact commands. Run
\code{scripts/verify.py} against that checkout to check patch applicability,
compile the prototypes and full patched copies, and record a fresh validation
result. The script leaves the checkout's source files unchanged. It expects
the listed baseline dependency modules to have already been built; this avoids
silently launching a full project build.

The original source remains authoritative. The two unified patches are intended
for review on an integration branch. The \code{patched/} copies make the
complete proposed modules easy to inspect. The full local toolchain, package
caches, and compiled objects are deliberately not included in the archive;
the pinned versions and commands are sufficient to recreate them.

title: Further research questions
source_text:
\section{Further research questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\item Can one small certified arithmetic-recipe interface cover the repeated
  coefficient families while retaining their distinct sharp bounds? The useful
  abstraction would expose a finite set of coefficient expressions and an
  explicit sign basis, rather than treating the final inequality as an opaque tactic call.
\item What is the best granularity of cached circuit equations? An indexed
  theorem minimizes declarations, while named intermediate equations cache
  normalization. A hybrid selected by actual downstream use may be better than
  either extreme.
\item Can the existing exponent-label checker be extended to additional
  arithmetic invariants, such as syntactic degree or coefficient support, with
  one shared local soundness theorem for circuit folds?
\item How much of the annotated checker can be expressed through one scanner
  invariant without obscuring arbitrary-raw-input soundness or changing the
  primitive-recursive code whose size is counted?
\item Which internal-natural algebra results can be transported through the
  established semiring interpretation, and which depend essentially on the
  object-language encoding and sealing machinery? A precise inventory would
  prevent both duplicate inductions and invalid external-to-internal shortcuts.
\item Can a parameterized cyclic-block library serve both the legacy and current
  arithmetic without making calibration-dependent assumptions implicit? The
  shared residue results are a small verified first step; masks and field
  positions should remain explicit data with proved interfaces.
\end{enumerate}

title: Executive assessment
source_text:
\section*{Executive assessment}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Executive assessment}

The best opportunities are concentrated in repeated mathematical interfaces:
encoded-list scanners, coordinate renamings, finite coefficient rows, and the
composition of already certified circuit blocks. A uniform substitution of
\code{simp}, \code{aesop}, or a larger heartbeat limit would miss these targets.

There are useful changes at three scales. First, seven private list-lookup
proofs can use two existing Lean-core lemmas; the supplied patch removes
40 physical lines. Second, a common arithmetic identity removes the
half-radix case analysis, and one row-wise argument can replace hundreds of
lines of repeated coefficient bounds. Third, the Split and Gap natural
circuits have an exactly matching 99-node suffix under a specified register
renaming. A reusable block for that suffix is the most concrete larger
architectural target identified here.

Some abstractions are worthwhile without shortening the file immediately.
For example, a common topological-DAG invariant theorem can replace repeated
strong inductions. After charging for the new helper, the first few clients
do not yet yield a net line saving. The report states this explicitly instead
of treating every abstraction as a compression result.

Several elementary examples were checked with the pinned Lean compiler.
Larger replacements and full scanner/circuit migrations have separate status
labels in Section~\ref{sec:validation} and the archive's verification record.
The strongest source comparisons are accompanied by scripts and exact data.

source_text:
\section{Move renaming out of expression evaluation}

\src{Representation}{ already provides \code{Expr.eval_rename}.}
However, \code{Rep.reindex}, both sides of \code{Rep.conjunction}, and both
sides of \code{Rep.disjunction} repeat the same assignment comparison:
rewrite expression renaming, apply congruence, prove function equality, and
split a sum index.

The useful common law is
\[
 \operatorname{natAssignment}(v,w)\circ\operatorname{Sum.map}(f,g)
 =\operatorname{natAssignment}(v\circ f,w\circ g).
\]
It gives the semantic rule:

\begin{Lean}
theorem eval_rename_natAssignment
    (e : Expr (σ ⊕ α)) (f : σ → τ) (g : α → β)
    (v : τ → Nat) (w : β → Nat) :
    (e.rename (Sum.map f g)).eval (natAssignment v w) =
      e.eval (natAssignment (v ∘ f) (w ∘ g)) := by
  rw [Expr.eval_rename, natAssignment_comp_sumMap]
\end{Lean}

The assignment lemma itself is proved by \code{funext i; cases i <;> rfl}.
The left and right witness layouts, using \code{Fin.castAdd} and
\code{Fin.natAdd}, become instances. The supplied
\code{AssignmentTransport.lean} contains the general law and both instances.

Orient simplification toward removing a renaming from the expression evaluator
and putting it in the assignment. Do not install both directions as simp rules.
Keep these rules local or in a small named collection until their effect on
other evaluators is clear. Coordinate constructors should expose their semantic
interface before the larger arithmetic expression is normalized.

This preserves executable representation data. In particular, replacing a
\code{Rep} constructor with an existentially chosen representation would lose
the point of the current design: \code{Rep} carries a specific expression
and finite witness count in \code{Type}. The desired refactor changes proof
fields while preserving those supplied data.

title: Replace half-radix case analysis with one identity
source_text:
\section{Replace half-radix case analysis with one identity}
\label{sec:radix}

\src{NativeCyclicRotation}{ defines a shifted digit by}
\[
 D_{\rho,s}(a,b)=(sa\bmod\rho)+\left\lfloor\frac{sb}{\rho}\right\rfloor,
\]
where $a=c(k)$ and $b=c(k-1)$. Its half-radix bounds analyze the possible
small digits separately. The arithmetic has a simpler normal form.

\begin{proposition}
For natural numbers $s,a,b$ with $s>0$,
\[
 D_{2s,s}(a,b)=s(a\bmod2)+\lfloor b/2\rfloor.
\]
Consequently, if $b\le3$, then $D_{2s,s}(a,b)\le s+1$.
If also $s\equiv0\pmod2$, then
\[
 D_{2s,s}(a,b)\bmod2=\lfloor b/2\rfloor.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Multiplication by $s$ commutes with remainder modulo $2s$, and positive
multiplicative cancellation gives $\lfloor sb/(2s)\rfloor=\lfloor b/2\rfloor$.
Now $a\bmod2\le1$ and $b\le3$ imply $\lfloor b/2\rfloor\le1$.
When $s$ is even, the first summand has even parity and the second is less
than 2, giving the final equality.
\end{proof}

The exact Lean proof of the identity is short:

\begin{Lean}
theorem step_eq (s a b : Nat) (hs : 0 < s) :
    step s a b = s * (a % 2) + b / 2 := by
  unfold step
  rw [Nat.mul_comm 2 s, Nat.mul_mod_mul_left,
    Nat.mul_div_mul_left _ _ hs]
\end{Lean}

\code{HalfRadix.lean} checks the identity, bound, and parity statement using
only Lean core and its proof-producing \code{omega} tactic. This is stronger
than the existing local bound: the current digit $a$ needs no upper bound;
only the predecessor $b$ is constrained. Existing public statements can remain
as corollaries, so callers need not change.

The distinction between generality and integration matters. This file proves
the scalar arithmetic used by the repository definition. It does not replay
the entire cyclic-rotation dependency chain or the later phase argument.
Specialization to $s=2^{88}$ is routine, but should still be compiled in the
original module before committing the replacement.

title: Compress the coefficient-row proofs without hiding their data
source_text:
\section{Compress the coefficient-row proofs without hiding their data}
\label{sec:rows}

\src{NativeCoefficientBounds}{ contains 22 private
\code{rowEnvelope_0}, \ldots, \code{rowEnvelope_21} lemmas.}
Between them, 158 leaves execute the same pattern:

\begin{Lean}
rw [abs_le]
constructor <;>
  linarith only [h0, h1, h2, h3, hsq, hmf, hkp]
\end{Lean}

Each row selects a finite piecewise coefficient expression, all bounded by
the same envelope. The large source block repeatedly copies the row function,
introduces the same three nonnegativity facts, splits its conditional tree,
and runs the same linear reasoning. The row data are fixed independently in
\src{NativeQuadraticParent}{.}

The direct refactoring is one theorem with a row index $k:\operatorname{Fin}(22)$.
Case-split $k$, reduce only the selected coefficient row, decompose the conditional
bounds, and close each arithmetic leaf using the shared facts. The
pair index stays symbolic; there is no need to enumerate all 528 unordered
pairs simply to prove a uniform magnitude bound.

\begin{Lean}
-- Schematic proof shape; the candidate is not kernel-verified.
have hsq := sq_nonneg (ports 0)
have hmf := mul_nonneg h3 h0
have hkp := mul_nonneg h1 h0
fin_cases k <;>
  dsimp only [rowCoefficient, Fin.reduceFinMk, Matrix.cons_val] <;>
  repeat' apply abs_ite_le
all_goals
  rw [abs_le]
  constructor <;>
    linarith only [h0, h1, h2, h3, hsq, hmf, hkp]
\end{Lean}

Controlled unfolding is essential. A global \code{simp} over the parent circuit
could unfold much more than these finite coefficient rows. An initial
\code{split_ifs} approach exceeded the simplifier's step limit on this input.
The revised proof keeps the existing small \code{abs_ite_le} lemma and descends
through the conditional bound structurally, without adding branch hypotheses.
Vector indexing is reduced before this step. The final verification receipt
distinguishes checking against exact extracted definitions from a full-module
replay.

The supplied whole-file candidate changes 679 physical lines to 130, a
549-line source reduction. This figure is a candidate source measurement;
its verification scope is stated separately. Removing private row wrappers
is permitted only after confirming they are not used externally. Keep the
public \code{abs_rowCoefficient_le_envelope} and later envelope theorem interfaces.

title: Do the same for coefficient naturality
source_text:
\subsection{Do the same for coefficient naturality}

\src{NativeNinePolynomial52}{ contains 22 private
\code{mapRowCoefficient} specializations.}
They establish that a ring homomorphism commutes with each row's coefficient
recipe. The mathematical reason is uniform: coefficients use integer literals,
addition, subtraction, multiplication, powers, and conditionals whose tests
depend on indices rather than ring values.

One finite-row dispatcher with the homomorphism simp laws can replace the
duplicated literal functions. A longer-term design stores the coefficient
recipe as syntax and derives naturality once by structural induction. Before
introducing new syntax, use the existing expression evaluators where suitable.
The independent theorem tying those recipes to the actual source rows must
remain: redefining the source row to equal its encoded coefficient sum would
remove the verification obligation instead of proving it.

The accompanying mapping candidate reduces its full file from 456 to 153
physical lines, a 303-line deletion. The combined isolated coefficient harness
was not verified: its last capped run timed out without diagnostics. Both
reductions therefore remain candidate source measurements, not completed
kernel-checked migrations.

title: A stronger abstraction: a finite majorant certificate
source_text:
\subsection{A stronger abstraction: a finite majorant certificate}

The envelope has the nonnegative monomial basis
\[
 m=(\beta^2,\ M_F\beta,\ M_C,\ M_F,\ \beta,\ K\beta,\ K,\ 1)
\]
with weight vector $b=(2,2,1,1,2,1,1,8)$. Each coefficient branch is an integer
linear combination $\sum_i a_i m_i$ with small integer $a_i$. Prove once that
$m_i\ge0$ and $|a_i|\le b_i$ imply
\[
 \left|\sum_i a_i m_i\right|\le\sum_i |a_i|m_i
 \le\sum_i b_i m_i.
\]
Then each concrete branch needs only a finite small-integer vector certificate.
This can serve multiple coefficient packages and reduces repeated arithmetic
reasoning more deeply than a compact tactic script. It is a proposed design,
not an implemented result. The basis must retain the existing linear dependence
on the large transport port $K$; an easier bound quadratic in $K$ would not
preserve the downstream published scale.

The corresponding Gap-family file demonstrates the better discipline. Two
particularly clear targets are:

\begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
\toprule
Theorem & Rules before & Rules after & Bytes before & Bytes after\\
\midrule
\code{natural_sourceSRegister} & 19 & 7 & 744 & 487\\
\code{natural_sourceRankRegister} & 36 & 9 & 1,142 & 555\\

The supplied patch changes the generator and generated output together.

\begin{Lean}

cuts[idx] = name
\end{Lean}

same mutable dictionary, its generated proof could see a later theorem or

on finding shorter rewrite lists. Regeneration, Lean checking, and downstream
checking are three distinct checks; the archive labels them separately.
